subject: English
topic: Reported Speech — Tense Backshift, Pronoun Change and Special Cases (W12 B1)

questions.stem: Change to indirect speech: He said, 'I am very happy.'

options.option_text: He said that he is very happy.
He said that he was very happy.
He said that I was very happy.
He told that he was very happy.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Key changes: (1) 'said' → 'said that' (no change, as there's no listener addressed). (2) 'I am' → 'he was' — pronoun 'I' → 'he' (speaker becomes third person); tense 'am' → 'was' (Present→Past backshift). Trap: 'he is very happy' = no tense backshift (wrong); 'I was very happy' = pronoun not changed; 'He told that' = 'told' requires an object (told me/him), whereas 'said that' is used without a direct object.

questions.stem: Change to indirect speech: She said to me, 'You look tired.'

options.option_text: She said to me that I looked tired.
She told me that you looked tired.
She told me that I looked tired.
She told to me that I looked tired.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Changes: (1) 'said to me' → 'told me' (when there is a listener, 'said to person' becomes 'told person'). (2) 'You' → 'I' (the listener 'me' becomes 'I' in reported form — the listener's perspective). (3) 'look' → 'looked' (tense backshift). Trap: 'She said to me that' = 'said to' should become 'told'; 'you looked tired' = pronoun not changed; 'told to me' = 'told' never takes 'to' before the person (told me, NOT told to me).

questions.stem: Change to indirect speech: They said, 'We will come tomorrow.'

options.option_text: They said that they would come tomorrow.
They said that they will come the next day.
They said that they would come the next day.
They told that they would come the next day.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Changes: (1) 'will' → 'would' (Future becomes Conditional in reported speech). (2) 'tomorrow' → 'the next day' (time expression change). (3) 'We' → 'they' (pronoun change). Trap: 'tomorrow' = must change to 'the next day' in indirect speech (tomorrow refers to the speaker's today, which has passed); 'will come' = no tense backshift (wrong); 'told that' = 'told' needs an object (told us), not 'told that'.

questions.stem: Change to indirect speech: He said to me, 'Where do you live?'

options.option_text: He asked me where did I live.
He asked me where I lived.
He asked me where do I live.
He said to me where I lived.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Indirect speech for WH-questions: 'asked + WH-word + subject + verb' (no inversion). Changes: (1) 'said to me' → 'asked me'. (2) 'do you live' → 'I lived' (no auxiliary 'do'; subject-verb order not inverted; tense: do→lived). Trap: 'where did I live' = auxiliary 'did' retained (wrong — in indirect speech, no auxiliary in statement order); 'where do I live' = no tense backshift AND auxiliary retained (doubly wrong); 'said to me where' = 'said' cannot introduce indirect questions.

questions.stem: Change to indirect speech: The teacher said to the students, 'Open your books.'

options.option_text: The teacher said the students to open their books.
The teacher told the students open their books.
The teacher told the students to open their books.
The teacher asked the students open their books.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Imperatives in indirect speech: 'told/asked/ordered + object + infinitive (to + verb)'. 'Open your books' → 'to open their books'. 'Your' → 'their'. The reporting verb is 'told' for direct orders. Trap: 'said the students to open' = 'said' cannot take a direct object before the infinitive; 'told the students open' = missing 'to'; 'asked the students open' = 'asked' is for requests/questions (appropriate here too), but still requires 'to': 'asked the students to open...'.

questions.stem: Change to indirect speech: She said, 'I have been waiting here for two hours.'

options.option_text: She said that she has been waiting there for two hours.
She said that she had been waiting there for two hours.
She said that she was waiting there for two hours.
She said that she had been waiting here for two hours.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Present Perfect Continuous → Past Perfect Continuous in indirect speech. 'Have been waiting' → 'had been waiting'. 'Here' → 'there' (place expression change). Trap: 'has been waiting' = no tense backshift; 'was waiting' = uses Past Continuous (loses the perfect continuous aspect); 'here' → must become 'there' (same location from reporter's perspective, which is different).

questions.stem: Change to indirect speech: He said, 'I was reading when she called.'

options.option_text: He said that he was reading when she had called.
He said that he had been reading when she called.
He said that he had been reading when she had called.
He said that he was reading when she called.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Both verbs in the sentence undergo backshift: 'was reading' (Past Continuous) → 'had been reading' (Past Perfect Continuous); 'called' (Simple Past) → 'had called' (Past Perfect). Both shifts are required since the reporting verb ('said') is past tense. Trap: 'was reading when she called' = no backshift at all; 'was reading when she had called' = only one verb backshifted (inconsistent); 'had been reading when she called' = only 'was reading' backshifted (inconsistent).

questions.stem: Change to indirect speech: He said, 'The Earth revolves around the Sun.'

options.option_text: He said that the Earth revolved around the Sun.
He said that the Earth is revolving around the Sun.
He said that the Earth revolves around the Sun.
He said that the Earth had revolved around the Sun.

questions.explanation: C is correct. EXCEPTION: Universal truths and scientific facts do NOT undergo tense backshift. 'The Earth revolves around the Sun' is a permanent scientific fact → remains in Simple Present: 'revolves'. Other exceptions: mathematical truths ('he said that two plus two is four'), historical facts often known (but not always exempt). Trap: 'revolved' = wrong — applying tense backshift to a universal truth; 'is revolving' = changes to continuous aspect (wrong).

questions.stem: Change to indirect speech: He asked her, 'When did you arrive?'

options.option_text: He asked her when did she arrive.
He asked her when she arrived.
He asked her when she had arrived.
He asked her when had she arrived.

questions.explanation: C is correct. WH-question indirect speech: 'asked + WH-word + subject + verb' (no inversion, no auxiliary). Changes: (1) 'you' → 'she' (listener becomes third person). (2) 'did you arrive' → 'she had arrived'. The Simple Past 'arrived' becomes Past Perfect 'had arrived' in reported speech (backshift from Past → Past Perfect). Trap: 'when did she arrive' = auxiliary 'did' retained and tense not backshifted (double error); 'when she arrived' = pronoun changed but no tense backshift; 'when had she arrived' = inversion retained (wrong — indirect questions use statement word order).

questions.stem: Change to indirect speech: He said, 'What a beautiful painting this is!'

options.option_text: He said that what a beautiful painting it was.
He exclaimed with admiration that it was a very beautiful painting.
He exclaimed that it is a very beautiful painting.
He told that it was a very beautiful painting.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Exclamatory sentences in indirect speech: use 'exclaimed (with admiration/joy/sorrow/surprise)'. Structure: 'exclaimed with admiration that + subject + was + very + adjective + noun'. 'What a beautiful painting' → 'it was a very beautiful painting' (adding 'very'; 'this' → 'it'). Tense backshifts: 'is' → 'was'. Trap: 'said that what a beautiful painting' = retains the exclamatory structure (wrong); 'it is a beautiful painting' = no tense backshift; 'He told' = 'told' requires a direct object person, not used for exclamatory conversion.
